title: Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam on Friday, IMD says
dek: The IMD has widened its forecast landfall zone and lowered its storm-surge estimate; Odisha has deployed 74 rescue teams and begun evacuations in its southern districts.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Cyclonic Storm Akvan barely moved over the Bay of Bengal on Tuesday, but the India Meteorological Department (IMD) widened the stretch of coast where it expects the storm to make landfall: in its 6.15 pm bulletin it said Akvan was likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on Friday, 20 November, as a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph. Its earlier bulletins had given the stretch as Nellore to Tuni.

The IMD lowered its storm-surge forecast to 0.6-1.3 metres above the astronomical tide, from up to 2 metres in the morning, and added Visakhapatnam to the six Andhra Pradesh districts where low-lying areas could be flooded. The storm is still expected to become a severe cyclonic storm on Tuesday evening and a very severe cyclonic storm on Thursday morning, bringing extremely heavy rain of 21 cm or more at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19 and 20 November.

## Latest bulletin

At 2.30 pm IST on Tuesday the storm lay near 12.3°N, 85.6°E, about 590 km east of Chennai, 650 km south-east of Machilipatnam, 650 km south-south-east of Visakhapatnam and 780 km south of Gopalpur, having moved north-north-west at 3 kmph over the previous six hours, the 6.15 pm bulletin said. Its forecast table shows winds of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph by 11.30 pm on Tuesday, 115-125 kmph gusting to 140 kmph by 11.30 am on Thursday and a peak of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph by 11.30 pm on Thursday, before the storm weakens to a severe cyclonic storm by 11.30 am on Friday and to a deep depression over land by Friday night.

The IMD warned of "major damage" to thatched and kutcha houses, power and communication poles, and standing crops and plantations in coastal Andhra Pradesh, waves of 9-14 metres from Thursday becoming "phenomenal" above 14 metres from Thursday night until landfall, and disruption to rail, road and air traffic. It advised a total suspension of fishing and offshore operations and that people living in coastal huts be moved to safer places.

Authorities have moved more than 80,000 people as a precaution, one report said, and National Disaster Response Force teams are on standby. Odisha, where heavy to very heavy rain is forecast in southern districts from 19 to 21 November, has deployed 74 rescue teams, 60 from its own disaster response force and 14 from the NDRF, in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri and Puri districts, and has begun moving people out of landslide-prone and low-lying areas, according to reports. Odisha's Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the government had made "full arrangements to secure lives and property", and the Ganjam district administration said 107 pregnant women had been moved to safety, reports said. IMD Director General Mrityunjay Mohapatra said Odisha was likely to get "heavy rainfall, but not extremely heavy rainfall", unlike during Cyclone Arnab, according to reports.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings in the 6.15 pm bulletin on Tuesday, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November; heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) on 19 and 20 November; heavy rain at isolated places in north coastal Andhra Pradesh on 21 November.
- Odisha: heavy rain at isolated places in south coastal Odisha on 18 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from 19 to 21 November.
- North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal: heavy rain at isolated places on 19 November.
- Rayalaseema: heavy rain at isolated places on 19 and 20 November.
- Eastern Telangana: heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: light to moderate rain at many places, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November.
- Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand: heavy rain at isolated places on 20 and 21 November; east Vidarbha and east Madhya Pradesh on 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and preparations

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest and westcentral Bay of Bengal until 20 November, the southeast and eastcentral Bay until 18 November, and the northwest Bay, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, on 19 and 20 November.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a review meeting at the Secretariat on Monday and directed officials to deploy National and State Disaster Response Force teams in advance, keep energy department staff ready to restore power, and divert floodwater into reservoirs, with round-the-clock monitoring from the state's real-time governance centre, according to reports. Odisha has alerted all 30 of its districts and opened round-the-clock control rooms, and district officials in southern Odisha have ordered the early evacuation of vulnerable people, reports said. In Tamil Nadu, the state's relief commissioner urged people to follow only official bulletins, after private forecasters circulated computer-model forecasts showing a landfall near Chennai; the IMD's track keeps the storm well off the Tamil Nadu coast.

## Background

Akvan is the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. The names used in the north Indian Ocean are drawn in sequence from a list contributed by 13 countries in the region; Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh, Murasu by India and Akvan by Iran, according to the published list.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast. The IMD's earliest outlooks pointed further north, towards the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; its bulletins since Monday have moved the expected crossing south, and on Tuesday evening it widened the window to run from Nellore to Visakhapatnam.

## What happens next

The IMD has moved from a pre-cyclone watch to a cyclone alert, the second of its warning stages; if the storm follows the forecast track it is expected to issue a cyclone warning, and then a post-landfall outlook, for the stretch of coast where landfall is expected. The landfall point may still shift; weather models differ on the storm's later movement and strength, according to reports citing the IMD's outlook.

## Key numbers

- 590 km: distance from Chennai at 2.30 pm IST on Tuesday
- 650 km: distance from Visakhapatnam
- Around noon, 20 November: forecast landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam
- 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 0.6-1.3 metres: forecast storm surge in seven Andhra Pradesh districts
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19-20 November
